\x3C/ul>\x3C/div>\x3C/figure>\x3Cp>\x3C/p>\x3Cp style=\"text-align: left;\">Which of the following statements must be true?\x3C/p>\x3Col style=\"list-style-type: upper-roman;\"> \x3Cli style=\"text-align: left;\">The median of data set A is equal to the median of data set B.\x3C/li> \x3Cli style=\"text-align: left;\">The standard deviation of data set A is equal to the standard deviation of data set B.\x3C/li> \x3C/ol>",rationale:"\x3Cp style=\"text-align: left;\">Choice A is correct. The median of a data set with an odd number of values that are in ascending or descending order is the middle value of the data set. Since the distribution of the values of both data set A and data set B form symmetric dot plots, and each data set has an odd number of values, it follows that the median is given by the middle value in each of the dot plots. Thus, the median of data set A is \x3Cmath alttext=\"13\">\x3Cmn>13\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>, and the median of data set B is \x3Cmath alttext=\"13\">\x3Cmn>13\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Therefore, statement I is true. Data set A and data set B have the same frequency for each of the values \x3Cmath alttext=\"11\">\x3Cmn>11\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>, \x3Cmath alttext=\"12\">\x3Cmn>12\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>, \x3Cmath alttext=\"14\">\x3Cmn>14\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>, and \x3Cmath alttext=\"15\">\x3Cmn>15\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Data set A has a frequency of \x3Cmath alttext=\"1\">\x3Cmn>1\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> for values \x3Cmath alttext=\"10\">\x3Cmn>10\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> and \x3Cmath alttext=\"16\">\x3Cmn>16\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>, whereas data set B has a frequency of \x3Cmath alttext=\"2\">\x3Cmn>2\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> for values \x3Cmath alttext=\"10\">\x3Cmn>10\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> and \x3Cmath alttext=\"16\">\x3Cmn>16\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Standard deviation is a measure of the spread of a data set; it is larger when there are more values further from the mean, and smaller when there are more values closer to the mean. Since both distributions are symmetric with an odd number of values, the mean of each data set is equal to its median. Thus, each data set has a mean of \x3Cmath alttext=\"13\">\x3Cmn>13\x3C/mn> \x3C/math>. Since more of the values in data set A are closer to \x3Cmath alttext=\"13\">\x3Cmn>13\x3C/mn> \x3C/math> than data set B, it follows that data set A has a smaller standard deviation than data set B. Thus, statement II is false.
